overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals clear viewer preference for extreme cosmic anomalies and hypothetical 'What If' planetary scenarios. Content featuring extreme planetary physics (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice, dark planets) generates the highest view counts and engagement velocity. Conversely, standard psychological facts and older historical/biological trivia show slower traction. We will pivot towards high-engagement space anomaly scenarios while introducing a fresh, unexploited cosmic phenomenon to capitalize on audience momentum.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved high views (1,029 and 972) with strong likes (38 and 18).
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-stakes immersive space scenarios focusing on bizarre exoplanet properties.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme environments like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) outperformed standard trivia significantly.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight rare, visually striking physical properties of newly discovered celestial bodies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts regarding common psychological tricks or brain facts (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 5AN7LUgqarc / 2fqaGqfsR4A) consistently garnered low views (<55) and zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks in favor of high-visual-impact space and physics content.
